name: D-Money
streamSlot: Mon–Fri · 9:00 AM–12:00 PM · Power Hour 2–4 PM
tagline: 10+ year NQ momentum trader — the 14/50/200 EMA stack tells him the trend, and he trades the retracement, never the breakout.
summary: D-Money (Damareous Young) is a 10+ year momentum day trader of NQ futures who trades prop-firm eval and funded accounts (Apex, Tradeify, Lucid) with Tradovate execution. His system pairs the 14/50/200 EMA stack with pure price action — exhaustion wicks, equal highs/lows, ORB, and mapped 1H/4H zones — entering on retracement rejections instead of chasing breakouts. He streams the 9 AM–12 PM session and is the desk's Power Hour specialist, live 2–4 PM every trading day.
oneLiner: Call the regime before the open (inside yesterday's range = chop, a break = expansion), then join momentum on 14 EMA retracement rejections — risking 10–20 points to make 50+.
keyQuote: Your job is not to pick the top. Your job is to join the momentum in whatever direction the market decides to go.
keyQuoteSource: Why You Can't Pick The Top On Nasdaq Futures
highlights: Join momentum — never pick tops or bottoms on expansion moves
Inside yesterday's range = chop; a break of it = expansion day
Enter only on retracement rejections at the 14 EMA with exhaustion wicks
Risk 10–20 points to make 50+ — his 11-for-55, 1:5 R:R math
One contract almost always; two only on an A+ entry with a 10-point stop
Cut early when the trade stops acting right; in chop, take the 50 and walk

videos.title: LIVE NQ Futures Day Trading at the BDH | DMONEY!
videos.takeaway: Daily live stream from the BDH trading floor: D-Money calls NQ setups in real time on prop accounts (Apex, Lucid, Take Profit Trader), narrating entries, exits, and mindset as they happen.

videos.title: If You Took This Trade You Got Paid
videos.takeaway: Shorted the retrace, called 28,200 live, watched it run 30+ points then stall eight short of the flush — took the rest for +$1,340. Waiting for the last eight points is how a winner becomes a round trip.

videos.title: I'm Not Chickening Out Of This One
videos.takeaway: "Two in the chamber" runner management: take most off, hold two contracts for at least 1:1 R — +$855 after a 50-point move. Saying out loud what you're tempted to do is most of how you avoid doing it.

videos.title: My Power Hour NQ Plan That Pays Before the Close
videos.takeaway: Power Hour is 3–4 PM (setup window 2–3): mark the ranges and the 1-hour 50 EMA beforehand, let the hourly candle open, then join momentum — and respect the 3:50 MOC momentum candle. "Power Hour isn't a setup. It's a window where volatility shows up more often than not."

videos.title: I Thought There Was More In The Tank
videos.takeaway: A failed re-entry ("felt like there was more in the tank... clearly there is not"), then patience paid: 20+ points on a banger, $1,100. Being wrong about how much was left isn't the problem — closing because of how it felt is.

videos.title: The 1 Hour Candles Look Like 1 Minute Candles
videos.takeaway: Bank-holiday playbook: 1-hour candles shrank from ~400 points to ~95, so low expectations and size down — expect a one-direction grind into a 1:00 PM close. "Compare today's candle size to last week's before you decide what size to trade."

videos.title: A 70 Point Candle In One Minute
videos.takeaway: Liquidity logic in 60 seconds: the move hunted the London low, failed, and turned for the London high — 25 points, +$535. When a move fails to take the obvious liquidity, the other side usually becomes the target.

videos.title: I Took It Before It Could Retrace
videos.takeaway: W pattern printed for 25–30 points; he took $1,335 off a $1,620 peak before the retrace. Exiting because you've hit a number and exiting because the move is done are different skills — the second one keeps the day green.

videos.title: I Waited For 28,500 To Break
videos.takeaway: Breakout-release trade at a pre-marked level: 15, 20, then 25 points "on a banger" — $970 on two contracts. Marking the level is the whole trade; everything after the break is just not getting in your own way.

videos.title: I Don't Blame You For Taking Profit
videos.takeaway: TP parked at 366, everything else on a 1-for-1; he held a two-in-the-chamber short through the pullback for $1,680. Wanting out and getting out are different decisions.

videos.title: Everyone Says EMAs Don't Work
videos.takeaway: The 14/50/200 EMAs defended: confluence, not signals — bearish cross at 9:20 AM, wide EMA spread = strong pressure, then the repeating drop-retracement-rejection short. They shine on trend days and underperform in chop.

videos.title: NQ Dropped 780 Points. Here's How I Traded It
videos.takeaway: CPI-day anatomy: equal highs swept at 30,852.75, a 245-point 8:30 candle, then all-day 14 EMA rejection shorts through ~780 points — flipping long when a candle closed back above the 14 for ~50 points. Pass evals on news days and lock them immediately.

videos.title: The Trend Is Your Friend. Here's What It Means
videos.takeaway: Buy the retracement toward the last higher low instead of chasing breakouts: 11-point stop vs ~55-point target — "risking 11 to make 55. Not exciting, just asymmetric." Every breakout in this session got retraced.

videos.title: What A 90 Point Bottom Wick Tells You
videos.takeaway: A 90-point bottom wick on the 30-minute open = heavy buyers below; buying the next candle as it dug back into the wick zone paid 50 points. Old wicks become reactionary levels — "always look left."

videos.title: The Double Bottom Was The Low All Day
videos.takeaway: ORB-breakdown short for 35, then a double bottom at ~31,144 called live held as the low all day; the best trade was a 30-minute bullish wick-candle long for 50. Took what the market gave — $3,235 and $1,830 on the cards, an eval passed.

videos.title: Why You Can't Pick The Top On Nasdaq Futures
videos.takeaway: After a 1,300+ point rally with one bearish 4-hour candle, shorting the top bankrupts you before NQ reverses — you run out of steam first. Buy retracements and use left-side resistance (31,040) only as a target, not a short signal.

articles.title: 10 Years In: What I'd Do Differently
articles.takeaway: Four lessons from 10 years: slow down to speed up, stop comparing payouts, start each day with a blank slate, and use the 1H/4H/daily charts (learned "by losing accounts"). It took two full years of losses before his first payout.

articles.title: Everyone Says EMAs Don't Work
articles.takeaway: The 14/50/200 EMAs are pure trend indicators for confluence, not blind signals. Bearish cross, wide spread, then the repeating drop-retracement-rejection short; below all three on the 1-hour, longs are "financial suicide."

articles.title: NQ Dropped 780 Points. Here's How I Traded It
articles.takeaway: CPI day: a 245-point 8:30 candle, equal highs swept at 30,852.75, then repeated 14 EMA rejection shorts through ~780 points and a 50-point "ending banger" long at 3 PM. Lock eval accounts the moment they pass.

articles.title: Inside Yesterday's Range Means Chop. Here's Why
articles.takeaway: Trading inside the prior daily candle means chop: he took the ORB downside break, scalped base hits off higher lows, and passed a $300k Apex eval making $15,000 at the open.

articles.title: The Trend Is Your Friend. Here's What It Means
articles.takeaway: Buy retracements near the previous higher low with the stop below it, targeting the prior higher high — an 11-point stop vs a 55-point target = 1:5 R:R "with practically no drawdown."

articles.title: What A 90 Point Bottom Wick Tells You
articles.takeaway: A 90-point bottom wick on the 30-minute open = heavy buyers below; buy the next candle digging back into the wick zone and ride the reversal. "Reactionary levels" are old massive wicks — they work even better on the 1-hour.

articles.title: The Double Bottom Was The Low All Day
articles.takeaway: ORB-breakdown short, then a double bottom at ~31,144 held as the absolute low of the day. Always cut a trade when the momentum dies; a heavy macro calendar (FOMC statement, Trump 1 PM) explains the slow grind.

articles.title: I Knew It Would Chop Before The Open
articles.takeaway: Fully inside yesterday's range = chop confirmed: the morning ORB short paid 126 points, then he hunted only base hits. Leave your ego at the door on inside-range days; expect consolidation ahead of NFP and earnings.

articles.title: Why You Can't Pick The Top On Nasdaq Futures
articles.takeaway: After a 1,300+ point rally with one bearish candle, you run out of steam before NQ reverses. Join the trend, buy retracements, and use left-side resistance only as a target zone, not a short signal.

articles.title: The Market Is Ranging More Than You Think
articles.takeaway: After an 84-point W-pattern pop, the afternoon became a 70-point ping-pong box: buy 14 EMA dips back to the top for "10, 15, or maybe 20 points tops." The market consolidates far more than it trends.

articles.title: How I Frame Quality Setups On Nasdaq Futures
articles.takeaway: Full real-time assembly of a 300+ point rally: look left, frame on the 30-minute chart with the stop below the prior candle low, ride repeated 14 EMA holds, exit at the 1-hour target zone. Talk through the chart out loud to slow your brain down.

articles.title: One Loss All Day On Nasdaq Futures
articles.takeaway: Bearish open inside yesterday's range preceded a 370-point melt: he shorted 14 EMA rejections, took one stop-out, then pivoted long when higher lows confirmed at 1:15 PM. One loss all day, +$1,655.

articles.title: The Nasdaq Ran 200 Points — Here's How I Traded It
articles.takeaway: A 105-point first 5-minute candle and price above yesterday's high = expansion brain. Longs off 14 EMA bounces toward 31,000; cut the chop fast ("Never sit and hope") and ride the consolidation breakout to the daily resistance block.

articles.title: My First Trade Today Was A Chop Trade. Keeping It Real
articles.takeaway: Honest recap of a no-follow-through range where even his first trade failed. Market truth: the vast majority of the time is consolidation — adapt with early profits, smaller size, and breaks.

articles.title: The Secret to Finding Reversals: Wick Analysis 101
articles.takeaway: Wicks "tell a story. They don't lie": swipe-and-go longs with stops below the rejection wick, and 14 EMA tap-and-reject shorts with ~20-point stops for 100+ point melts. Higher-time-frame wicks carry far more power.

articles.title: Lost My First Trade, Then Caught The Biggest Move Of The Day
articles.takeaway: Opening long chopped and cut immediately, then flipped short for 120+ points and banked 50. Formula: "Cut your losers quickly, follow the momentum, and let the winners run!"

articles.title: Stop Trading Your Bias: How I Survived This Choppy Open
articles.takeaway: The first 15-minute candle's massive bottom wick was the clue; when the ORB low was swiped and reclaimed, shorts were done. Never bring a directional bias into the morning — liquidity hunts come before the real drop.

articles.title: Trading Psychology: Why I Stayed Flat On A Difficult Day
articles.takeaway: After a 300-point rip and 350-point dump, the afternoon was a suffocating barcode — he finished flat and called it a win. Scale size down, force nothing, and don't let boredom pick your trades.

articles.title: Surviving The NQ Chop: My Live Trading Breakdown
articles.takeaway: Took the +50-point ORB long and applied the chop rule: when the market gives you 50 points, take them off the table. News-heavy weeks keep institutions sidelined — take what you can get and survive the chop.

articles.title: The Reality of Trading: 2 Stops, Then a Massive Trade
articles.takeaway: Two controlled 10–15 point stop-outs, then a short flip and a 150+ point higher-low reversal ride. Small controlled losses let you pivot into the real move of the day.

articles.title: Don't Let Greed Kill Your Trade: Cut Early
articles.takeaway: Chopping a trade early is a tool, not failure: exit for 5–10 points and re-enter when price behaves. Exit triggers: exhaustion wicks against you, and new 30-min/1H candles that retrace first.

articles.title: How I Find A+ Entries Using the EMAs (NQ Futures)
articles.takeaway: The A+ entry: as close to the EMA as possible after push, retracement, and exhaustion-wick rejection — 10–20 point stop, 50+ point target. Miss the push? Wait for the wave to recede to the EMAs.

articles.title: How Many Contracts Should You Actually Trade? (Position Sizing)
articles.takeaway: One NQ contract almost exclusively: on a $50K account with a $2,000 trailing drawdown, a 20-point stop = $400 = five losing trades of ammo. Two contracts only on an A+ EMA-wick entry with a 10-point stop, keeping dollar risk identical.

articles.title: Why Most Traders Miss the Reversal (And How I Spot It)
articles.takeaway: Three reversal clues: pin bars after extended downtrends, equal highs/lows (often swiped once to trap breakout traders), and structural higher lows after big drops. Context is everything — patterns only count when "the rubber band is stretched thin."

articles.title: My Full AM Trading Routine (Before I Take Any Trade)
articles.takeaway: The daily sequence: mark yesterday's high/low, map the first 5-minute ORB, read pre-market context, then wait for the break-and-retracement before entering. A rigid bias is "an appetite for destruction."

articles.title: How I Trade Price Action and Momentum Together
articles.takeaway: Price action = what price did at levels; momentum = candle body size. The A+ assembly: 1-hour macro sets the bias, then wait for the 5-minute drop into the 14/50 EMA retest and the top-wick rejection.

articles.title: How I Spot Equal Highs and Equal Lows for Reversals
articles.takeaway: Two clustered candles topping/bottoming within one point: equal highs stall bulls (short signal), equal lows are hard floors (long while they hold). Often swiped once before reversing — slow down and check the exact wick prices.

articles.title: What Is Momentum Trading? My Full Breakdown
articles.takeaway: Momentum = who is in control, read from candle size: an 80–130 point "Bazooka Candle" out of consolidation means institutions picked a side. The first hour prints 100–130 pointers; lunch kills momentum.

articles.title: How I Trade a Range When NQ Is Stuck in Chop
articles.takeaway: Map the box with rectangles over the wicks (ranges run 30–85+ points), buy the absolute bottom, short the absolute top, stops 10–15 points beyond the edge. Every range eventually breaks — flip back to momentum on the retest.

articles.title: What Timeframes I Actually Trade (and Why)
articles.takeaway: Analyze on 1H/4H, execute on 5-min/15-min because 1-hour stops would be 80+ points: "15-point risk... targeting a massive 150-point profit." Watch the clock before hourly closes and the 1-hour rubber band.

articles.title: How I Trade the Opening Range Breakout (ORB) Strategy
articles.takeaway: Map the first 5-minute candle wick-to-wick (15-minute for the more reliable version), enter the break with the EMAs behind it, or take the early/retest entries. Stop beyond the EMAs or breakout candle; target the nearest left-side level.

articles.title: How to Identify a Trend Day Before It Happens
articles.takeaway: Trend-day tells: huge solid candles in the first 5–30 minutes, price holding beyond all three EMAs all session, and clean HH/HL (or LH/LL) structure. Entry is always the retracement-to-EMA rejection, never the extreme.

articles.title: My TradingView Setup: EMAs, Boxes, and Tools Explained
articles.takeaway: Exact chart config: EMAs at 14/50/200, transparent rectangle zones, black horizontal lines reserved for ORB, the price-range tool for exact measurements, arrows for engulfing/rejections — executing through TradingView's Tradovate integration.

articles.title: How I use the 14, 50 and 200 EMA to Trade NQ Futuress
articles.takeaway: The foundational EMA guide: lagging confluence tools best on 1H/4H/daily; match entry-timeframe crosses to the higher-time-frame direction. Stops go on the opposite side of the EMA — tight by construction, and a break through it invalidates the trade anyway.

articles.title: How I Map Out Support and Resistance Levels (NQ Futures)
articles.takeaway: Draw zones, not lines: 1H/4H rectangles from wick to candle body at historic turning points. Zones are take-profit targets, gap fills are reaction levels, and a consolidation break through a box flips resistance into support.
